steps.title: Prepare reagents and solutions
steps.instruction: Gather all chemicals and instruments with catalog numbers: urethane (Product No. U2500, Merck) – dissolve 0.5 g ml⁻¹ in double‑distilled water; heparin sulphate (1000 IU ml⁻¹, Biological Evans Ltd.) – freshly make heparinised saline by mixing 1.0 ml heparin with 50 ml 0.9 % NaCl to obtain 20 IU ml⁻¹; histamine dihydrochloride (Product No. H7250, Sigma) – prepare a 1000 mM stock in distilled water, store 2–8 °C, dilute to 10 mM with 0.9 % NaCl before each experiment; Castroviejo corneal scissors, 4.5″ curved blade (Model No. 4336853428, Kretzer); Optivisor® magnifying head loop (Model No. 633096000519, Donegan Optical); double‑ported 24 G polyethylene cannula (lab‑made); BP transducer, bridge amplifier and Power Lab 26T data acquisition system (AD Instruments®).

steps.title: Anesthetize the rat
steps.instruction: Use healthy adult male albino rats (Charles‑Foster strain, 202.5 ± 12.5 g) housed at 28 ± 2 °C, 12:12 h light/dark, with food and water ad libitum. Inject urethane solution intraperitoneally at 1.5 g kg⁻¹ into the left lower abdomen 1 cm lateral to the midline. Keep the animal in a calm, dark environment. Re‑assess anaesthesia every 15 min by testing corneal reflex (cotton wisp) and paw withdrawal reflex (blunt forceps); give an additional 50–100 mg urethane if reflexes are present.

steps.title: Perform tracheostomy
steps.instruction: Shave the anterior neck, make a midline skin incision, and expose the deep cervical fascia. Identify and laterally retract the thyroid gland. Separate the strap muscles along the midline to expose the trachea. Pass a thread beneath the trachea, make a small transverse nick between the 5th and 6th tracheal rings with a blade, insert an appropriately sized polyethylene tube, and secure it tightly with the thread, keeping the tube length minimal. Cover the incision with cotton moistened with normal saline and aspirate secretions as needed.

steps.title: Expose right femoral triangle
steps.instruction: Shave the skin over the right femoral triangle. Make a small incision at the midpoint of an imaginary line joining the urethral orifice and the hip joint. Dissect through superficial fascia and extraperitoneal fat to reveal the femoral vessels. Ligate the superficial epigastric artery and retract the fat superiorly.

steps.title: Isolate femoral structures
steps.instruction: Using a glass seeker, separate the femoral artery, femoral vein and femoral nerve from each other and pass individual threads around each structure for retraction and manipulation.

steps.title: Cannulate femoral artery
steps.instruction: Dissect approximately 1 cm of the femoral artery and place a proximal thread clamp. Make a small nick distal to the clamp with the Castroviejo corneal scissors (Model No. 4336853428). Fill the double‑ported 24 G polyethylene cannula with freshly prepared heparinised saline (20 IU ml⁻¹) and insert it retrogradely into the artery. Secure the cannula to the arterial wall with threads. Perform all steps under 2.75× magnification using the Optivisor® (Model No. 633096000519).

steps.title: Connect recording equipment
steps.instruction: Attach the horizontal port (HP) of the cannula to a blood‑pressure transducer, then to a bridge amplifier, and finally to the Power Lab 26T data acquisition system for real‑time MAP display. Place ECG needle electrodes in standard limb‑lead II configuration (right arm, left leg, ground). Secure a curved needle to the skin over the xiphisternum, connect it via a thread to a force transducer, and link this to the same data acquisition system to record respiratory excursions.

steps.title: Prepare and instill histamine
steps.instruction: Dilute the 1000 mM histamine stock to the desired experimental concentration (1 mM, 10 mM or 100 mM) with 0.9 % saline. Load 100 µl of the histamine solution into the vertical port (VP) of the cannula. Ligate the ipsilateral femoral vein to prevent outflow. Instill the 100 µl retrogradely (against blood flow) into the local arterial segment.

steps.title: Record cardiovascular‑respiratory parameters
steps.instruction: Continuously monitor and record mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR) and respiratory frequency (RF) from the acquisition system. At the end of the experiment, inject 1 ml of air into the quiescent lung through the tracheal tube, note the resulting deflection (x), measure the average amplitude of respiratory excursions (h) over a 5‑s interval, and calculate respiratory minute volume (RMV) as (h / x) × RF.

steps.title: Determine paw water content
steps.instruction: After euthanasia, disarticulate both hind paws at the ankle joint. Weigh each paw wet, then dry them in an electric oven at 90 °C for 72 h. Weigh again and calculate water content as [(wet – dry) / wet] × 100 %.
